item.title: Re: Psychological Theories in 1800s
item.content:encoded:
Sent you a PM.

In short, psychotherapy for mental illness (and even modern conceptions of mental illness as something with (partially) psychological and relationship-based causes rather than just a moral, spiritual, or physical cause) did not exist until the 1880's. Some of the people who Freud worked under in the 1880's were experimenting with hypnosis for "hysteria", but Freud was the first person to have a systematic theory and practice of therapy.

Before that in the 1800's, even the idea that mental illness had a physical/neurological cause, or the idea that people with mental illness might get better if you talk to them/don't treat them like complete shit/don't chain them up, were new ideas.

In terms of theories, most people were still basing theories on philosophy, most were interested in "normal" functioning people rather than mental illness, and the field of medicine itself was way less developed than it is now. Early psychologists were also more interested in studying "normal" perception and consciousness than abnormal psych (but, again, didn't exist as a separate field of study until the 1870s).

"Animal Magnetism" was a theory in the 1700's/early 1800's that led into hypnosis, but that was a theory of general human health/functioning and wasn't applied to mental illness until the 1880's. You could look at the Humors and Phrenology for ideas before that, but again, these were physical theories (with physical treatments in the case of humors) not "therapy."

Here are some links:
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigmund_Freud
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodor_Meynert
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Martin_Charcot
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Pinel

https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_psychiatry (read the early modern part)

Edit: Also, the British aristocracy really cratered because of WW1, so you're free to set your SCP in the 1890-1910 range. If you do that, here are a few other things to look at:
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightner_Witmer
https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Kraepelin

item.title: Re: Help. I posted my SCP but it says access denied.
item.content:encoded:
Alright, so what you have to do is go to the series page in question, and scroll to the bottom of the page. There, you should be able to see a series of red buttons; the furthermost one on the left being the word "edit". Click that, and scroll through the edit box to the slot № that you applied your article to ( * [[[SCP-5129]]] - [ACCESS DENIED] ).

Delete the text that says "[ACCESS DENIED]" and add whatever title you want. Do not change anything else on the page. Once finished, you can click save, and that's it. For the .aic elements like Secretary_Helen or CROM, it may take around 5 minutes to update, but Wikidot will do so instantly.

However, this piece is really quite rough around the edges. The sections written in blue appear to describe the desired version of the anomaly associated with its designation, but I got the sense that the anomaly's form is dependent on its own perception of its current name's connotations. Aside from the mechanics of the anomaly itself, I feel like the description and conprocs could have been more fleshed out and served as more of a hook for the article, as basically my only incentive to continue reading (prior to the addenda) was to see how it was connected to the region which shall remain unnamed. I'm also not really a fan of "access granted" being formatted as all lowercase, nor a single footnote that says "holly" as opposed to "Commonly known as holly" or something of that sort.

Clever, but unpolished. Novote.

item.title: The Jukebug
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror
Page Format: I plan to use the standard page format, adding in interviews and audio logs to tell the stories of three separate cases.

Elevator Pitch: An auditory cognitohazard that latches onto the brain waves of a person until the afflicted person hears a “catchy" song. Once the afflicted has a song stuck in their head, the anomaly perverts the lyrics to encourage the afflicted to act out intrusive thoughts. The anomaly can lie dormant for up to three days without a song to embed itself into, before eventually dissipating. The anomaly can be detected through basic brain activity scans, appearing in the shape of an insect on images of the brain. If a song is introduced that the afflicted finds catchy, the anomaly will stay undetected by the afflicted for two more days. During which it will play the song excessively in their mind. Anytime the afflicted sings the song, their brainwaves are modified to transmit the anomaly into the minds of others, starting a separate cycle. After the two day infection period, the anomaly begins to goad the original afflicted. The more the afflicted resists, the harder it pushes with symptoms ranging in severity. The Foundation can eradicate the anomalous brain activity by playing music that lacks (in the opinion of the listener) pleasant rhythm or rhyme, for 18 hours.

It is unclear if this anomaly is merely a phenomenon or an entity. No evidence of an entity occupying the physical body of any afflicted people exist, other than vivid descriptions of a singing insect-like creature seen during the REM cycles of the afflicted, in the first several days of exposure. The vivid and consistent descriptions of this creature, coupled with the insect-shaped brain image, have lead to a dichotomy in the observing staff. Those who believe it is merely a phenomenon, which the evidence seems to support the most, have developed the current SCP protocols. A separate team, continues to search for evidence of what they call the “Jukebug.”
Central Narrative: Multiple accounts of different instances of the “Jukebug,” including: the aftermath of a child's birthday party, a surgeon, and a musician working on their newest song.

Hook: I think the idea that you could have been infected by this SCP and it’s already too late is spine-chilling and compelling enough to draw people in.

Additional Notes: Since the anomaly spreads due to divergent brainwaves of a person during the recitation of the song in their mind I am not sure if this is actually an auditory cognitohazard or not.

item.title: SCP Idea - Livin' on a Prayer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Emotional

Page Layout: Containment » Description (Place of discovery, appearance, known history) » anomalous effects » explorations

Elevator Pitch: SCP is supposed to be about human's pilgrimage to become better person hidden under intend to gain human's deepest desires.

Central Narrative: SCP is mummified fragmented corpse of man with engravings on his whole body. When human comes in contact with part of corpse, part of corpse individual got in contact merges with their own body part or replaces body part if it's missing, having appearance of host's own body part with engravings from corpse. Once it happens part that merged with corpse is now between 2 dimensions. It can influence our dimension and even dimension which corpse connects to. Once the corpse is fully gathered and merged with host, individual mirrors actions (harm included) done in SCP dimension except movement, yet the person is unable to directly communicate with our dimension. In order to separate host from corpse, host's body has to be cooled down to 32 °C (89.6 °F) which will cause corpse to separate and could be pulled off from host with no harm.

Then pilgrimage will start.
Pilgrimage could be described as 7 tests on human mind which are connected to 7 deadly sins. Through the pilgrimage tested person is influenced by shape shifting entities taking form of things important to tested individual and questioned by snake like entity. It points on flaws in human personality showing that nobody is perfect. It's supposed to be dark as it seems like way to become better person, but it only leads to certain death.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I don't know. I've seen many awesome SCP against which my idea couldn't stand a chance, but I took this as opportunity to show my ideas and who knows…someone might like it and find it unique. This SCP was made from my daily thoughts so I don't find it too interesting.

Additional Notes:

In this SCP appears my personal scientist Doctor Alistair Lovecraft.

item.title: Re: Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Siners
item.content:encoded:
+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

I think I can very quickly summarize this as, 'generic biblical-themed pay-for-your-sins anomalous punishment object.' It falls into the Series 1 trope of being a thing that does a thing and exists for seemingly no reason other than what it is.

The Central Narrative is a very long extension of the Elevator Pitch, which is where the anomalous description is supposed to go. Because of this, this SCP essentially has no story.

I'm very much fascinated by religious and spiritual imagery and themes as well as the psychological aspect of it all. The idea of an SCP that makes people own up to their sins or get #rekt otherwise is some that innately appeals to me, as it portrays humanity in its purest, rawest form. However, this is as generic as generic gets. It might as well be God descending on random people and telling them to git gud or git fucked.

Apologies if this was harsh. To be fair, the anomaly works. It's kinda bland, but almost any anomaly can work nowadays if you attach a good enough story to it.

Tell you what. Here's a suggestion. You know what would make this work? Showing us someone going through its trials and tribulations. Considering how character-focused this anomaly innately needs to be, make a character(s), flesh them out, and have them undergo its trials. Forget test logs. This thing doesn't need them. One or two people will be enough to show off its obvious effects.

Show us someone at their lowest low before they come up. Or, ya know, having then go even further down. I think two characters would be best for this since you'd want to show us the good path and the bad path.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a good day. 👍

Forum thread: Awaiting Greenlight / The Book of the Siners

item.title: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy, maybe some Emotional Aspects (only very few)

Elevator Pitch: A warehouse which has anomalous properties that could give it the thaumiel classification and which produces all kinds of objects that share that sentiment. They all have way too many drawbacks and weaknesses and are branded as failures by researchers (safe class instead of thaumiel) because of that.

Central Narrative:The warehouse gets discovered and testing ensues. At first the researchers are enthusiastic and hopeful of being able to find anomalies with which they might be able to contain really hazardous or hard to contain SCPs but get gradually more and more frustrated as their research shows what a waste of time this warehouse and its contents are. This is expressed through researcher notes and letters send to higher-ups, asking for reassignment to other SCPs.
I am also thinking about adding a small sad note that this SCP produces at the end, which explains that it just wants to help. This would however reclassify this anomaly as Euclid since it is sentient so i would leave that part out.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: So far, i personally haven't seen a thaumiel object that gets rebranded as safe (only ones that got neutralized) or an anomalous object which promises to be helpful but turns out useless in every way

Additional Notes: Some ideas of objects this SCP produces are:
-a cardboard box, which is able to lock anything inside of itself, but is way more flammable than normal cordboard, making it spontanously combust
-a pair of glasses which protects from visual cognitohazards but degrades eyesight until total blindness
-a hazmat suit which makes you immune to any disease while wearing it. After taking it off you are plagued by many lifelong alergies

No sandbox has been created at the time of posting.
English is not my first language, so please tell me if my grammar is terrible or my vacobulary sucks.
This is also my first SCP.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Ok, I have edited the post based on your feedback. I wasn't really sure of what singular part of his name to call him. I suppose I could stick with Twist.

Originally, I thought it best to put down the introduction to his story to build intrigue rather than blatantly put down the entirety of what I plan to do for the article. I had put down a lot more information earlier but that exceeded the word count limit.

The core concept of this character does not lie with hunting down and killing Jack. That's just how Twist ended up being discovered. Its what happens after the SCP foundation gets a hold of Twist that makes up what this article is about. Jack is a part of Twist's mind and is Twist's motivation for escaping the foundation. Take him out of the equation and Twist is very cooperative, answering questions and participating in experiments when allowed. While the SCP foundation's involvement prior to his capture is extremely minimal, the article isn't about the capture so much as it is about the SCP foundation's attempts at containing Twist and learning from him.

The LLUN aura is the source of Twist's anomalous nature and is what gives Twist his various abilities. It is designed to be a mystery for readers to uncover upon reading the article and subsequent experimentation/interview logs.

One of Twist's abilities is his ability to look at something and instantly obtain information about that something's purpose, function, how it works, and how to eliminate it. The LLUN aura prevents Twist from divulging information about anything that might reveal information about the LLUN. It is the main antagonizing force within this article as the SCP foundation struggles to get as much information out of Twist as possible, seeing as Twist can contain secret knowledge about ANY SCP creature that he comes into contact with.
